title: mos.tray.v1
description: Outcome of a tray-control verb emitted by `mos tray <action> --json`: the first commands mos issues that CHANGE drive state (eject/close via START STOP UNIT 0x1B, lock/unlock via PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL 0x1E). Mechanism facts only — mos reports what the command did and does NOT unmount for you (the deliberate contrast with `drutil tray eject`'s policy). A command the drive ANSWERED is success (the process exits 0) even when the outcome is a refusal; a transport/lock failure (drive mounted or held by another client, gone, IO) emits mos.error.v1 and a non-zero exit instead. Design: doc/research/2026-06-13-tray-control-feasibility.md; encoding: T10 04-349r1.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node of the current media, or null when the drive is empty (an eject of an empty tray is still a valid command).

registry_id.description: Drive service IORegistry entry ID — attachment identity. 0 = unavailable. NOT durable: replug mints a new ID.

action.description: The control verb issued. eject/close are START STOP UNIT (LoEj=1, START=0/1); lock/unlock are PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL.

force.description: eject only (null on every other action): true when --force was requested. Every eject GRACEFULLY unmounts a mounted disc first (DADiskUnmount, Whole, NOT Force) and then ejects; mos NEVER forces the filesystem, so a busy volume (open file handles) surfaces as mos.error.v1 busy on both the default and --force. macOS arms a tray Prevent lock when it mounts a disc and that lock survives the unmount, so the DEFAULT eject clears both Prevent states after its own unmount and ejects (Finder/drutil semantics) — that OS mount-lock is not a deliberate one. --force extends the lock-clearing to a COLD lock: a deliberately-locked idle drive with no mount in play (a robot's tray lock), which the default eject returns as outcome refused_locked. The one blocker neither clears is another userland client holding exclusive access (no SCSI preempt): mos.error.v1 code exclusive_access.

outcome.description: done = command completed GOOD. refused_locked = CHECK CONDITION 53/02 MEDIA REMOVAL PREVENTED — an eject/close hit a Prevent lock (a reported fact, not a CLI failure; on the default eject this is a COLD deliberate lock, since the OS mount-lock is auto-cleared after the graceful unmount). The sense KEY is contextual and does not gate this: 05 (ILLEGAL REQUEST) with media present, 02 (NOT READY) on an empty drive. refused_other = any other answered CHECK CONDITION (e.g. a drive without Persistent Prevent support rejecting the persistent state with 5/24/00). already_locked = `lock` on a MOUNTED disc: the lock CDB can't issue (media still mounted) but a mounted disc is already removal-locked by macOS, so the requested state already holds — a success, not a busy error.

sense.description: SCSI sense triple the drive returned on a refusal, or null. Populated for any answered refusal — refused_locked is always asc/ascq 53/02 (the sense key is 05 with media present, 02 on an empty drive); refused_other carries whatever the drive reported (e.g. 5/24/00 INVALID FIELD IN CDB for a drive without Persistent Prevent support), so a consumer can diagnose a non-lock refusal. Always null on done.

key.description: Sense key, 0x-prefixed hex (e.g. 0x05 = ILLEGAL REQUEST). Same representation as mos.state.v1 / mos.event.v1.

asc.description: Additional Sense Code, 0x-prefixed hex (e.g. 0x53 = MEDIA REMOVAL PREVENTED).

allOf.title: force is a boolean only for eject
